subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only or self-deny tool policy for per-agent orchestration, and what syntax and security semantics should become the first public contract?
rationale: The current implementation is intentionally non-escalating, while the requested behavior changes config/API and command/file delegation boundaries that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept delegate-only config
options.body: Add a narrow selfDeny or equivalent field that hides tools only from the parent model surface while preserving ordinary deny-wins policy for real denials and requiring explicit delegated access.

options.title: Route through per-spawn policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open until the sessions_spawn child-tool allowlist work lands, then reassess whether parent self-deny is still a separate product need.

options.title: Decline core exception
options.body: Document that strict orchestrators must use separate agent profiles and that tools denied to a parent cannot be delegated through that parent.

recommendation.title: Accept delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a narrow selfDeny or equivalent field that hides tools only from the parent model surface while preserving ordinary deny-wins policy for real denials and requiring explicit delegated access.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a public config and security-boundary direction rather than a narrow bug in one helper.
